svg.aria-label: How to write ح، خ، ج: 3 letters, ح, خ, ج, one after another
svg.title: Writing ح، خ، ج
svg.desc: 3 letters written one after another: ح, خ, ج (arabic). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoNaskhArabic-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ح: Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet: ج ح خ, independent Haa at 00:00–00:01 (University of Oregon Libraries Open Textbook, 2023) <https://opentext.uoregon.edu/introarabic/chapter/%D8%AC-%D8%AD-%D8%AE/>; خ: Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet: ج ح خ, independent Khaa at 00:02–00:04 (University of Oregon Libraries Open Textbook, 2023) <https://opentext.uoregon.edu/introarabic/chapter/%D8%AC-%D8%AD-%D8%AE/>; ج: Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet: ج ح خ, independent Jeem at 00:05–00:06 (University of Oregon Libraries Open Textbook, 2023) <https://opentext.uoregon.edu/introarabic/chapter/%D8%AC-%D8%AD-%D8%AE/>. Source notes on variation: ح: The page's Haa attachment demonstrates independent ح in two pen-down runs. The clip opens with the first mark already underway: visible motion lengthens the short left stem downward from 00:00.00–00:00.15. After a pause, the pen lifts once and restarts near the stem's upper portion at 00:00.32, sweeping down-right and around the bowl without another lift through 00:00.82. The adjacent lesson identifies haa as a two-way connector and separately prints its contextual shapes. Unlike the adjacent Jeem demonstration, there is no dot stroke; this stem-first order is source-specific rather than inherited from ج. The learner path fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh outline while preserving Arabic provenance. خ: The page's Khaa QuickTime clip demonstrates independent خ body-first at 00:02.8–00:03.9: the short upper head travels left-to-right, then the same pen-down run turns downward and curls around the bowl. The pen lifts once and places the single dot above at 00:04.2–00:04.4. The adjacent lesson identifies khaa as a two-way connector and separately prints its contextual shapes. Although the body resembles ج and ح, this order comes from Khaa's own clip: it matches adjacent Jeem's body-first run rather than Haa's separately demonstrated stem-first restart. The learner path fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh outline while preserving Arabic provenance. ج: The cited Jeem demonstration draws the independent body first at 00:05.1–00:05.8: a short upper head travels left-to-right, turns downward at the right, and curls back left into the rounded bowl without lifting. After the body is complete, the pen lifts once and places the dot below at 00:06.3–00:06.5. The adjacent lesson identifies jeem as a two-way connector and separately prints its contextual shapes. This independent learner path fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh outline; its Arabic body-first provenance remains separate from the Urdu dot-first record for the same Unicode glyph.
svg.text: How it is written — 3 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 2 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 3 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet: ج ح خ, independent Haa at 00:00–00:01 (University of Oregon Libraries Open
Letter 2: stroke order after Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet: ج ح خ, independent Khaa at 00:02–00:04 (University of Oregon Libraries Open
Letter 3: stroke order after Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet: ج ح خ, independent Jeem at 00:05–00:06 (University of Oregon Libraries Open
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
